result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A and B use the same sorted diverging-bar design, so the choice comes down to details. A puts the percentage labels right next to each bar and marks Northfield clearly with an '0.0% (on plan)' label. B draws Northfield as a tiny gray sliver and puts its values in a column far from the bars. B does better at labelling the zero line 'Plan' and has an axis with gridlines, but A is easier to read at a glance. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both are diverging bar charts sorted by % gap from plan, with a blue/orange split and matching totals. B puts each percentage right at the end of its bar, labels the 'Behind plan' and 'Ahead of plan' directions over the zero line, and marks Northfield as '0.0% (on plan)'. A shows Northfield as a thin gray sliver and puts its numbers in a separate column away from the bars, so B reads a little faster.
